musts.section: SA-1 session.boundary-blackbox-note (build_now) — CLI vs schema/kernel field location
musts.issue: `scaffold_blackbox_note_session` (used by `glosa session open`) and `cmd_session_close` write `session_id`, `session_boundary`, `entry_anchor`, `retention_note` NESTED under a top-level `"session"` wrapper key (cli/glosa:844-856, :894, :907-930). But `schema/blackbox_note.schema.json:13-31` defines `session_id`/`session_boundary`/`entry_anchor` as TOP-LEVEL properties of the note (no `session` object at all in the schema), and `kernel/glosa_kernel.py`'s `check_session_boundary_reset()` (glosa_kernel.py:1487-1516) — the exact cross-file function the patch/spec name as the SA-1 acceptance-test mechanism ("two Blackbox Note files sharing session_id split by a real process restart both carry ai_state_at_boundary literal 'reset'", FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md:69-70, SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md §8) — reads `note.get("session_id")` / `note.get("session_boundary")` at the TOP level. A note produced by the shipped `glosa session open` therefore has `sid = None` from `check_session_boundary_reset`'s point of view and is silently skipped (`if not sid: continue`), so the SA-1 acceptance test the patch certifies as build_now/ready-to-apply is not actually enforceable on the real CLI output path. The mismatch is invisible to both test suites because they encode the two different, incompatible conventions separately: `tests/test_install.py:184-185` asserts the NESTED shape (`data["session"]["session_id"]`), while `tests/test_kernel.py:1503-1516` and `tests/sim/corpus/v04/blackbox/*.json` (e.g. `retention_undeclared_valid_005.json`) use the TOP-LEVEL shape the schema/kernel actually implement.
musts.fix: Pick one field location and make it consistent everywhere: either (a) flatten `scaffold_blackbox_note_session`/`cmd_session_open`/`cmd_session_close` to write `session_id`/`session_boundary`/`entry_anchor` at the top level of the blackbox_note instance (matching the schema and `check_session_boundary_reset`), and update `tests/test_install.py` accordingly, or (b) change the schema and `check_session_boundary_reset` to read a nested `session.*` object and update `tests/test_kernel.py`/`tests/sim/corpus/v04/blackbox/*` to match. Either way, add a test that actually round-trips a `glosa session open`-produced note through `check_session_boundary_reset` (not just schema validation) to catch this class of drift.
musts.reason: Verified directly against the files. cli/glosa:844-856 (scaffold_blackbox_note_session) and cmd_session_close (~894-930) write session_id/session_boundary/entry_anchor/retention_note nested under a top-level `session` key. schema/blackbox_note.schema.json:13-31 defines session_id, session_boundary, entry_anchor as TOP-LEVEL properties -- there is no `session` object in the schema at all. kernel/glosa_kernel.py check_session_boundary_reset (~1487-1516) reads note.get('session_id') and note.get('session_boundary') at top level and explicitly documents that "notes without a session_id ... are silently skipped." A note produced by `glosa session open` has session_id=None at the top level from this function's perspective, so it is silently skipped -- meaning the SA-1 cross-file acceptance check the patch (FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md:69-70) and spec (SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md §8) name as the enforcement mechanism cannot actually fire on real CLI output. This split is exactly mirrored in the two test suites: tests/test_install.py:184-185 asserts the nested shape (data["session"]["session_id"]), while tests/test_kernel.py:1503-1528 and tests/sim/corpus/v04/blackbox/retention_undeclared_valid_005.json use/assume the top-level shape that the schema and kernel actually implement -- so neither suite would catch a note produced by the real CLI failing the kernel check. This is a genuine spec-code fidelity break in the SA-1 build_now acceptance mechanism, not a stylistic SHOULD: the acceptance test the patch certifies as enforceable is not enforceable on the shipped CLI's own output. MUST upheld.

musts.section: schema.retention-direction-field Session-object field (SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md §2.1, P18 table) — candidate_set_deltas[]
musts.issue: `design/SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md` §2.1's Session-object table and `methodology/P18_session_architecture.md`'s mirrored table both list `candidate_set_deltas[]` as a field that "lives on" `hypothesis_selection.yaml`, sourced from the build_now (score 8) proposal `schema.retention-direction-field`. No such field exists anywhere in `schema/hypothesis_selection.schema.json` (verified by full read), `kernel/glosa_kernel.py`, `cli/glosa`, or any test/data file in the repo (repo-wide grep for `candidate_set_delta` returns zero hits outside the design docs). Unlike the sibling gaps this same patch discloses (HU-2's remaining sub-fields, the missing `chi_recip` CLI subcommand — both named explicitly in `CHANGELOG.md`'s "Still genuinely not built this pass" list), this specific spec node carries no TODO, no deferral note, and no CHANGELOG entry anywhere — a rule-10 ("no finding is ever dropped"/every spec node traceable to code, TODO, or explicit deferral) violation.
musts.fix: Either add `candidate_set_deltas[]` to `schema/hypothesis_selection.schema.json` (or wherever it is meant to live) with a kernel/CLI wiring, or add an explicit TODO/deferral (in the schema's own $comment and CHANGELOG.md) naming it as unbuilt, matching the discipline already applied to the other named gaps in this pass.
musts.reason: Verified directly. `schema/hypothesis_selection.schema.json` (full read) has no `candidate_set_deltas` field, and neither `kernel/glosa_kernel.py`, `cli/glosa`, nor any test/data file references it (repo-wide grep zero hits outside the two design docs naming it in their Session-object tables). Crucially, this is unlike the sibling gaps the finding contrasts it with: HU-2's remaining sub-fields and the missing `chi_recip` CLI subcommand are both explicitly named in CHANGELOG.md's 0.4.0 entry ('Still genuinely not built this pass ... outside this task's ownership'). `candidate_set_deltas[]` gets no such treatment anywhere: (1) the DAG_v0.4.yaml node `schema.retention-direction-field` (design/SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md ~line 234-239), which both §2.1's table and P18's table cite as this field's source, lists `fields_added: [retained_direction]` only — `candidate_set_deltas` is not in its target/fields_added, build_now or otherwise; (2) CHANGELOG.md's 0.4.0 'Built this pass'/'Still genuinely not built this pass' accounting explicitly names `retained_direction` as already-shipped but never mentions `candidate_set_deltas` in either direction; (3) FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md §11.3 and its flag-rules table cover only the distinct, sibling cooking-log-level `candidate_set` field (kernel.candidate-set-delta-cooking-step, correctly marked `with_revision` there) — not the hypothesis_selection-level `candidate_set_deltas[]` array the finding is about; (4) the schema file's own $comment blocks give explicit provenance/status prose for every other field sourced from the same `schema.retention-direction-field`/SA-2 proposal (`session_id`, `chooser_reaffirmations`, `retained_direction`, `direction_evidence_relation`) but say nothing about `candidate_set_deltas` at all. So this spec node genuinely has no code, no TODO, no CHANGELOG entry, and no deferral note anywhere in the repo — the rule-10 violation the finding describes is real and is a MUST (release-blocking traceability gap), not a SHOULD.

shoulds.issue: Both `design/SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md` §10.2 and `design/FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md` §9 state this proposal's entire kernel-rule deliverable as: "standard jsonschema.ValidationError (missing required key / enum mismatch) — no custom kernel message needed, pure declarative schema constraint." The shipped code instead adds a new, unrequested mechanism — `defeater_status_for_card()` plus kernel rule31 (`_rule31_defeater_status_warning`) — a derived `untested|tested_survived|tested_defeated` classification with a WARNING fired once a card's status has advanced past Draft with an empty `defeater_log`. This is real, useful, well-disclosed-in-comment code, but it is scope beyond what either spec document authorized for this proposal id, and neither `design/FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md` (the design-of-record for this pass) nor `design/SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md` was updated to reflect that the shipped kernel rule is broader than what was specified.
shoulds.fix: Add a short note to `design/FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md` §9 (or a follow-up patch entry) disclosing that rule31/`defeater_status_for_card` is additive scope beyond the originally-specified pure-schema-constraint deliverable, citing its own rationale (already well-argued in the code comment at kernel/glosa_kernel.py:1053-1068) so a reader of the design docs alone isn't misled about what the kernel rule actually does.

shoulds.issue: `design/FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md` §10a names `methodology/data/non_defeater_phrase_table.json` (sibling to `contaminated_concept_table.json`) as the target file for rule29's phrase list. That file does not exist; the regex (`_STRENGTH_OF_CLAIM_RE`) is kept inline in `kernel/glosa_kernel.py` instead. The deviation is honestly disclosed in the kernel's own code comment (glosa_kernel.py:969-971: "is NOT in this task's ownership list, so the pattern is kept inline here instead"), so this is a minor documentation-vs-code drift rather than a silent gap, but the patch document itself was never updated to match.

musts.issue: schema/blackbox_note.schema.json:13,18,32,91 declares session_id, session_boundary, entry_anchor and question_trace as TOP-LEVEL properties of a blackbox_note, and kernel/glosa_kernel.py's check_session_boundary_reset (line 1499-1516, reads note.get('session_id')/note.get('session_boundary')) and tools/blackbox_log.py's question_trace_coverage (line 164, reads note.get('question_trace')) both read them at the top level. But cli/glosa's scaffold_blackbox_note_session (line 808-857) and cmd_session_close (line 900-934) — matching templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml:100-131 — nest all of these fields under a second-level `session:` object instead (data['session']['session_id'], etc.). Verified empirically: running scaffold_blackbox_note_session() twice with the same session_id and passing both notes to kernel.check_session_boundary_reset() returns ok:True with zero errors, because note.get('session_id') is None for both (the real value sits at note['session']['session_id']) — SA-1's whole cross-file reset-enforcement mechanism silently never fires on any note the CLI actually produces, and question_trace coverage checking is equally blind to CLI-produced notes.
musts.fix: Pick one home and make schema, template, CLI, and kernel agree: either (a) drop the `session:` wrapper in cli/glosa and templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml and write session_id/session_boundary/entry_anchor/question_trace/retention_note as top-level note fields matching schema/blackbox_note.schema.json's actual property definitions, or (b) move the schema definitions of those four properties (and update check_session_boundary_reset/question_trace_coverage to read note.get('session', {}).get(...)) under a `session` sub-object. Then add a regression test that exercises `glosa session open` twice with a shared --session-id and asserts check_session_boundary_reset actually reports an error when ai_state_at_boundary is missing/wrong, not just that it returns ok on well-formed input.
musts.reason:
Confirmed by direct file inspection and execution. schema/blackbox_note.schema.json:13,18,32 defines session_id, session_boundary, and entry_anchor as TOP-LEVEL properties (session_boundary's own description even says "the session boundary + AI-reset fact lives here, not in a new artifact"). kernel/glosa_kernel.py:1487-1516 check_session_boundary_reset reads note.get('session_id') and note.get('session_boundary') at the top level. But cli/glosa's scaffold_blackbox_note_session (~line 832-857) and cmd_session_close (~900-934), matching templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml:100-131, nest session_id/session_boundary/entry_anchor/retention_note under a second-level `session:` object, and even the top-level `session_ref` field the CLI does populate uses a different key name than schema's `session_id`. I reproduced the failure empirically: built two notes via scaffold_blackbox_note_session sharing session_id='SESS-X', forced note1's nested session.session_boundary.ai_state_at_boundary to 'carried' (a real violation), and ran kernel.check_session_boundary_reset([n1,n2]) -> {'ok': True, 'errors': []} because note.get('session_id') is None for both, so they never land in the same group and the check is a silent no-op on every CLI-produced note. This is a genuine one-fact-one-home MUST, not a SHOULD: SA-1's cross-file reset-enforcement mechanism exists specifically to catch this class of violation and structurally cannot fire on real CLI output.

One correction to the finding's scope: the question_trace part is overstated/inaccurate. Schema line 91-92 and templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml:68-77 vs 117-119 explicitly document TWO deliberately distinct fields (top-level question_trace = per-turn trace inside one note, §9.1 scope; session.question_trace = Problem Card refs opened this session, SA-3 scope) — not the same fact duplicated in two homes. I verified tools/blackbox_log.py's question_trace_coverage is not "equally blind": it reads the correct, by-design top-level field and instead produces a false-positive gap error on any CLI note with question-kind lines, regardless of whether the separate session.question_trace is properly filled — a real but different and lesser gap (CLI never scaffolds/prompts for the optional top-level per-turn trace), not a location-mismatch duplicate of session_id/session_boundary/entry_anchor. The finding's core issue and fix direction (pick one home, align schema/template/CLI/kernel for session_id/session_boundary/entry_anchor, add a regression test asserting check_session_boundary_reset actually errors on a real violation) are correct and necessary; the question_trace clause should be dropped or rewritten as a separate, narrower finding rather than folded into this one.

musts.issue: §16's rule-numbering table states the python kernel rule ceiling before this pass was 28 and this pass adds only rule29 and rule30 — presented as 'the full ledger this pass'. But kernel/glosa_kernel.py actually ships a rule31 (_rule31_defeater_status_warning, lines 1053-1107) this same pass, invented as a NEW mechanism (a derived defeater_status field + WARNING) that design/SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md §10.2 explicitly said this proposal (lrs.defeater-defeated-status-field / lrs.defeater-log-required-outcome-enum) did NOT need: 'standard jsonschema.ValidationError ... no custom kernel message needed, pure declarative schema constraint' (spec §10.2, and FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md §9 itself repeats the same 'no custom kernel message needed' line). rule31 therefore has no founder_decision_needed row, no citation in the patch's own build list, and is missing from the 'full ledger' table that is supposed to be authoritative.
musts.fix: Add rule31 to §16's table (and to the §10/§16 narrative) with its own citation, tier, and founder_decision_needed status, or — if rule31's added derived-field mechanism was not actually approved by any proposal — flag it as an out-of-scope kernel addition requiring a founder decision before it ships, per the same discipline the patch applies to every other new rule.
musts.reason: Verified directly against the files. kernel/glosa_kernel.py:1053-1107 ships `_rule31_defeater_status_warning`, explicitly commented as "Kernel rule31 (lrs.defeater-defeated-status-field, design/SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md §10.2)" and wired into the validator at lines 1245-1248 (adds to `warnings`). But SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md §10.2 (lines 373-377) for that exact proposal (`lrs.defeater-defeated-status-field`, part of `lrs.defeater-log-required-outcome-enum`) states: "Error string: standard jsonschema ValidationError (missing required key / enum mismatch) — no custom kernel message needed, pure declarative schema constraint." FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md §9 (line 230) repeats verbatim: "no custom kernel message needed, pure declarative schema constraint" for the same lrs id. Yet rule31 is a bespoke Python function computing a derived `defeater_status` and emitting a custom WARNING string — not a jsonschema declarative constraint — contradicting the very spec section it cites as its source. Checked §16's "Rule numbering table (full ledger this pass)" (FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md:484-491): only rule29 and rule30 appear in the "new this pass" column for the python kernel rules row; rule31 is absent — confirmed by grep, zero hits for "rule31" anywhere in FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md. rule31 also has no founder_decision_needed row and is not listed in the patch's own build/citation list (§9, §10). This is a genuine MUST: an undisclosed, unauthorized kernel addition that contradicts its own cited spec section and is missing from the ledger table that document §16 claims is "the full ledger this pass," violating rule 10 (no finding dropped / full traceability) and the one-fact-one-home discipline.

shoulds.issue: schema/blackbox_note.schema.json's `entry_anchor` (line 32-35) is a plain string ref to a problem_card id (the H0 term only), matching design/SESSION_ARCH_v0.4_SPEC.md §2.1's Session-object row. But FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md §6 and methodology/P18_session_architecture.md line 35/61-63 both describe a DIFFERENT, not-yet-built `entry_anchor` — a five-conjunct sub-object {unresolved, existing_evidence, change_condition, verification_intent, resistance_route} planned on schema/problem_card.schema.json's intake object. The same field name is used for two structurally different things on two different schemas. The patch is careful to disambiguate the rule29/flag-rule29 same-number collision explicitly (§16) but never flags this same-name/different-shape collision for entry_anchor, which is exactly the class of duplicate-homes confusion the LENS on this review calls out.
shoulds.fix: Rename one of the two fields (e.g. keep blackbox_note.entry_anchor as the H0 problem-card ref, and name the planned problem_card sub-object something distinct like intake.entry_h0 or intake.pre_exposure_anchor) and add an explicit disambiguation note in FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md §6/§16 the way rule29 vs flag-rule29 already gets one.

musts.section: SA-1 session-boundary mechanism (kernel rules 29-31 area / check_session_boundary_reset)
musts.issue: `scaffold_blackbox_note_session` (used by `glosa session open`) writes ALL session-boundary facts nested under a top-level `"session"` key (`session.session_id`, `session.session_boundary.ai_state_at_boundary`, `session.entry_anchor`, `session.question_trace`, `session.retention_note`, etc. — cli/glosa:844-856), and `templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml:100-133` documents the same nested shape. But `schema/blackbox_note.schema.json` defines `session_id`, `session_boundary` (with the `ai_state_at_boundary` enum:["reset"] constraint), `entry_anchor`, and `question_trace` as FLAT TOP-LEVEL properties (confirmed: schema has no `session` property at all — `python3 -c "import json; print('session' in json.load(open('schema/blackbox_note.schema.json'))['properties'])"` -> False). `kernel/glosa_kernel.py`'s `check_session_boundary_reset` (line 1487-1516) and every test exercising it (`tests/test_kernel.py:1503-1528`) read the flat top-level `note.get('session_id')` / `note.get('session_boundary')`, never `note['session'][...]`.
musts.fix: Because `schema/blackbox_note.schema.json` has `additionalProperties: true`, a note produced by `glosa session open`/`glosa session close` validates cleanly while its `session_boundary.ai_state_at_boundary` enum constraint (the whole point of SA-1's `ERROR: ai_state_at_boundary missing or not literal 'reset'` control) is never checked, and `check_session_boundary_reset(notes)` silently treats every CLI-produced note as having no `session_id` at all (`sid = note.get('session_id')` is None, so `if not sid: continue` skips it — see kernel/glosa_kernel.py:1502-1503). SA-1's own "MUST fire" failing control is trivially evaded by the tool built to implement it, on every real note it produces. Pick one shape (flat, matching schema/kernel/tests, or nested, matching CLI/template) and make all four artifacts agree; add a test that runs `check_session_boundary_reset` on the actual output of `scaffold_blackbox_note_session`/`cmd_session_open`+`cmd_session_close`, not only on hand-built flat fixtures.
musts.reason: Directly reproduced end-to-end. (1) schema/blackbox_note.schema.json properties are flat top-level: session_id, session_boundary, entry_anchor, question_trace (confirmed via python json load — no 'session' key exists), with additionalProperties:true. (2) cli/glosa:844-856 scaffold_blackbox_note_session (used by `glosa session open`, cli/glosa:880-896) and templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml:107-119 both nest these same facts under a top-level `session` key (session.session_id, session.session_boundary.ai_state_at_boundary, session.entry_anchor, session.question_trace). (3) kernel/glosa_kernel.py check_session_boundary_reset (line 1487-1516) reads only flat `note.get('session_id')` / `note.get('session_boundary')`; tests/test_kernel.py:1503-1528 exercise it only with hand-built flat fixtures, never against real CLI/scaffold output. Live repro: ran `python3 cli/glosa session open --project testproj --human-owner tester --session-id sess-verify-1 --entry-anchor GLOSA-PC-fake --out-dir /tmp/glosa_test`, which produced a note whose `self_check` (schema validation via run_check) returned ok:true/PASS/no errors despite the enum-constrained ai_state_at_boundary living only under the unvalidated nested `session` key. Then loaded that exact note and called `check_session_boundary_reset([note, note])` directly (same session_id repeated, which would trip SA-1 if flat session_id/session_boundary existed) — it returned ok:true with zero errors, because `'session_id' in note` is False at top level. This reproduces on the actual tool output, confirming SA-1's 'MUST fire' control is fully inert for every note the CLI produces, exactly as the finding describes. This is a MUST (core safety/architecture control silently non-functional on all real usage), not a SHOULD, and the proposed fix (unify the shape across schema/kernel/tests vs CLI/template, and add a test against real scaffold+cmd_session_open/close output) is the correct remedy.

musts.section: FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md §5 (hu.mastery-gate-wired) citation vs. actual FOUNDATION_v0.6.md state
musts.issue: §5 states: 'FOUNDATION target: §7.5, replace `"Unchanged from v0.1 §7.5"` (line 1621) — that pointer is broken...' — a rule-17 file:line citation asserting `design/FOUNDATION_v0.6.md:1621` currently reads `"Unchanged from v0.1 §7.5"`. Direct read shows `design/FOUNDATION_v0.6.md:1619-1631` already contains the FULL replacement text ("Fixed (`hu.mastery-gate-wired`, HU-1, ... build_now): this pointer previously read 'Unchanged from v0.1 §7.5' ...") — i.e. the fix this patch proposes as not-yet-applied is already present on disk in the file the patch cites as still broken. This also contradicts the patch's own scope note (line 4-7): 'It does not itself edit ... design/FOUNDATION_v0.6.md ... per this task's ownership scope.'
musts.fix: Re-verify FOUNDATION_v0.6.md's current §7.5 content before citing it; either the citation is stale (someone already applied this exact fix out-of-band, in which case §1/§5/§15 of the patch and the DAG node `hu.mastery-gate-wired` should be marked done/superseded rather than `founder_decision_needed: true`), or two different documents named FOUNDATION_v0.6.md exist and the wrong one was read — either way this is a rule-17 citation-accuracy failure that must be corrected before this patch is treated as an accurate diff-to-apply.
musts.reason: Confirmed by direct read. design/FOUNDATION_v0.6.md is the only such file in the repo (find confirms no v0.1 or duplicate exists), and its §7.5 (lines 1619-1631) already reads \"Fixed (`hu.mastery-gate-wired`, HU-1, ... build_now): this pointer previously read 'Unchanged from v0.1 §7.5' ...\" — i.e., the exact replacement text FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md §5 (line 138) proposes to apply is already present on disk. The patch's line 138 citation asserting the broken pointer is still live at FOUNDATION_v0.6.md:1621 is stale/inaccurate, and this also contradicts the patch's own preamble (lines 4-7) claiming it does not edit FOUNDATION_v0.6.md — since v0.6.md already carries the fix, either it was applied out-of-band without updating this patch's citations/status, or the patch was drafted without re-reading the current file state. Either way this is a rule-17 (cite file:line accurately) violation in a MUST-tier wiring item (HU-1), and the node's `founder_decision_needed: true` / \"ready to apply\" framing is inconsistent with the target section already containing the applied text. This is not a SHOULD — a broken/stale citation underpinning a MUST-tier gate-wiring decision, and an internal self-contradiction between the patch's stated scope and the observed file state, blocks release under rule 17 and rule 10 (traceability) until corrected: either mark hu.mastery-gate-wired done/superseded or explain the discrepancy (e.g., two work streams touched the same file) explicitly in the patch.

musts.section: SA-1 session boundary (CLI + template vs. schema)
musts.issue: `scaffold_blackbox_note_session` (and `cmd_session_close` at line ~924) write `session_id`/`session_boundary`/`entry_anchor`/`question_trace`/`human_retained_residue_ref`/`retention_note` NESTED under a top-level `"session": {...}` key. But `schema/blackbox_note.schema.json` defines `session_id`, `session_boundary`, `entry_anchor`, `question_trace` as TOP-LEVEL properties (confirmed by direct read of the schema's `properties` object), and `kernel/glosa_kernel.py`'s `check_session_boundary_reset` (line 1487) reads `note.get("session_id")` / `note.get("session_boundary")` at the top level too — matching `tests/test_kernel.py`'s own fixtures (lines 1511-1528), which set `note_a["session_boundary"]`/`note_b["session_boundary"]` at the top level, not nested. Any Blackbox Note produced by `glosa session open`/`glosa session close` therefore has `session_id` absent at the location the kernel actually checks, so `check_session_boundary_reset` silently skips it entirely ("notes without a session_id are not part of any group") — the exact SA-1 boundary-reset enforcement the design docs (FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md §1, P18_session_architecture.md TODO) claim to have built is a no-op for every note the shipping CLI actually produces. `templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml:100-131` documents the same wrong nested shape (comment: "additionalProperties is true on this schema, so this block validates today without a schema-file change" — true only because the schema silently ignores the misplaced block, not because it is checked). This is a live one-fact-one-home violation of the exact kind §2.2/P18 explicitly say they are preventing: the same fact (`session_boundary`) now has two candidate homes, one enforced (schema top-level) and one silently inert (CLI/template nested `session:` block).
musts.fix: Rewrite `scaffold_blackbox_note_session`, `cmd_session_open`, and `cmd_session_close` in cli/glosa to set `session_id`, `session_boundary`, `entry_anchor`, `question_trace`, `human_retained_residue_ref`, `retention_note` as top-level keys on the note dict (matching schema/blackbox_note.schema.json and kernel/glosa_kernel.py's check_session_boundary_reset), and fix templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml's `session:` block to the same flat, top-level shape. Add a regression test (a note produced by `glosa session open`/`close`, fed straight into `check_session_boundary_reset`, must actually be checked) so this class of drift cannot recur silently.

But cli/glosa's scaffold_blackbox_note_session (~line 807-855) and cmd_session_close (~line 900-935) nest all of session_id/session_boundary/entry_anchor/question_trace/human_retained_residue_ref/retention_note under a top-level \"session\": {...} dict — confirmed by direct read of both functions. templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml:99-131 documents the identical nested shape, with a comment stating \"additionalProperties is true on this schema, so this block validates today without a schema-file change\" — verified true (schema additionalProperties is indeed True), and this is exactly what makes the nested block schema-legal but functionally invisible to check_session_boundary_reset. musts.issue: `scaffold_blackbox_note_session` sets `ai_state_at_boundary` to the value `"carried"` when `carried_from_ref` is given (`"carried" if carried_from_ref else "reset"`), and `templates/knowledge/blackbox_note.yaml:111` documents the same two-value scheme (`reset | carried`). But `schema/blackbox_note.schema.json`'s `session_boundary.ai_state_at_boundary` enum is `["reset"]` only (single literal, no `"carried"` value exists), and its own description cites `sources/notes/EPISTEMIC_FUSION_v7.1.txt:328` — "m^{AI}_{s+1,0} = 0 (by architectural scope definition)" — meaning AI state resets at EVERY boundary, unconditionally, regardless of whether the human explicitly retains something. `design/FOUNDATION_v0.7_PATCH.md` §1 and `P18_session_architecture.md`'s own Session-object table state `ai_state_at_boundary` as "fixed literal `reset`" with no second value. The CLI/template's `"carried"` state conflates "the human explicitly retains residue" (a fact that already has its own field, `human_retained_residue_ref`) with "the AI itself carries state forward" — precisely the collapse the session-boundary architecture (and NC-58, AIContribution≠EpistemicResponsibility) exists to prevent. Since this value is also written into the mis-nested `session:` block (see the sibling finding above) it currently escapes schema enum validation entirely, so nothing catches it today.
